rationale:
`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[exceptions]` takes a parameter named `errors`, so it is a site of `requirements.ci.errors`. It collects validation errors for a repository check. It does not abort authoring.

Violation matches:
- **`return Ok(BTreeMap::new())`:** This runs only when `crate::evidence::load_definitions` fails. The function first pushes that error into `errors`, so the failure is reported. The remaining work is `citation_items(root, &definitions, ...)` and the per-item review validation, and both need the loaded definitions. The checks skipped by the return therefore depend on the failed check's result. `collect_references(root, errors)` runs before the return, so its errors are kept. The caller `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[check_saved]` carries on afterwards: it runs `discovered_files` and the per-file and per-function checks with the same `errors`. The requirement allows this exit, because a failed parse or load counts as one failed check and independent checks still run.
- **`continue`:** This skips items that have no `habeas:coverage` citation. Skipping them is not a failure, so no error is hidden. It also skips nothing that a failure left undone.

Inside the loop, an item whose review file is missing gets one finding. An item whose review file exists gets `validate_review`. Either way `errors.extend(findings)` runs, and there is no early exit between checks in an iteration. One failure per item is pushed once. `check_saved` also removes duplicate messages with `errors.retain(|error| seen.insert(...))`, so a failure is not reported twice. I found no gap.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
